title: Research: prove completion-free projectors for PR #1736's mixed-width bit slots
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR1736 leaves projector compatibility of its mixed width-seven/eight placements open. This package shows that every retained placement for k=0,...,74 keeps the entire local q-perp block in one slot or in the remainder. The builder packs a contiguous prefix starting at zero, and its first slot has width at least seven. A general prefix lemma therefore extends this account's PR1307 completion-free projector argument to these particular mixed placements.

The audit checks 296,325 representative helper slots and 166,500 child/copy partitions, with zero local splits, and preserves all 75 committed idle histograms. The 32-replica product accounts for 9,482,400 helper occurrences across alternative scenarios; it is proved by an injective family index, not independently replayed per replica. All 111 rational port projectors are checked. A rank/window-preserving split of k=1's first two width-seven factors gives different individual projectors under two rational completions while preserving their aggregate child.

This is a scoped geometric proof plus finite certificate, not a width-seven provider, a new price, a packing optimum, supplier admission or kappa claim. Package: `research/bit-mixed-width-projectors/`; the proof is `PROOF.md`, with read-only `RESULT.json` replay. Selected records and frozen predecessors are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Task card:

- **Task ID / scope key:** `bit-helper-contract` / `bfb61f829a81535adeae`, refined to `PR1736/mixed7-8/prefix-packed/q-perp/no-completion`. Chooser nonce `8cd45dd933439a35e236a028d99f1a85`, track `bit-mechanisms`, priority revision 4.
- **Base commit:** `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Exact predecessors: incorporated PR1736 `b4fd72163234c164d9a05f2f7dac9c57dcd7fb66`; PR1307 `4cb255ef445e2abc3ff8845fa01210b974e2cf6c`; selected PR589 `a5afc8c6169ea61ba7c51dfd3cade02cc7b13b46`. No pending implementation dependency. Every consumed main file has an exact Git blob and SHA256 in `SOURCES.json`.
- **Concrete object/question:** PR1736's actual `wopt.solve(k, Fraction(1,570), True)` plus `verify.build` placements, all 75 k values, all 111 ports, nine stages and replica-local families. Do individual factors need a local orthonormal completion?
- **Scope status:** changed. The original H2/K scalar examples have retained semantic-D coverage; this takes PR1736 Open next question 3 and PR1307 Open next question 2 instead. It is a hosting-interface sublemma.
- **Changed restriction:** extend PR1307's selected width-eight census to the specified mixed-width prefix placements. Width alone does not establish a split.
- **Method/domain:** exact rational projector algebra, independently checked source levels/windows and masks, typed role coverage, all remainders, a general prefix proof and finite mutation controls. No new candidate search or optimization claim.
- **Nearest overlap:** PR1736 supplies the placements and prices; PR1307 supplies the retained geometry argument; PR1281 supplies the window-free relaxation. PR2423's concurrent geometric audit is on the distinct R438 width-eight allocation, and the current class-U P111 plane-upgrade investigation concerns a different decoder object. PR2465's deletion ladder was considered but its slack pattern already has PR1281 coverage, so that work was not repeated.
- **Full cost / observable improvement:** every existing rank charge is retained and no operation is added. The required improvement is a discharged geometric sub-obligation, not a lower numerical bill. Physical conversion costs remain open.
- **Success/stop test:** source-bound complete coverage or an explicit split/counterexample, then verification and handoff within the bounded session. The 75-case certificate completes that scope.
- **Artifact/reproduction:** `python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-mixed-width-projectors`; predecessor credit below.

The [claim is in discussion #1289](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1289#discussioncomment-18953091). The final shared-snapshot overlap check covered 812 open PRs including drafts (2026-10-15 16:22:35 UTC) and 1,276 Discussion records (16:27:10 UTC), with complete pagination. Queries included the task card, `1736`, `width7-windows`, `mixed-width projector`, `q-perp split`, and adjacent packing terms. Cached/offline warnings were retained; arbitrary diffs and unindexed closed work are not covered. No-match results are not novelty certificates.

Canonical main was fetched again at 2026-10-15 16:26:44 UTC and remained the exact base above. Guidance, priority revision, selected result and all consumed files were unchanged. The full local card and refresh decision are retained in `TASK.json` without changing historical source pins.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, Linux x86_64, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-mixed-width-projectors --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-mixed-width-projectors
python3 -I -O -B research/bit-mixed-width-projectors/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/bit-mixed-width-projectors/test_verify.py
```

The first two commands passed in the checkout. Both optimized scripts passed in a Git-free relocated export containing only the package and declared inputs. Expected audit marker:

```text
PASS_BIT_MIXED_WIDTH_PROJECTORS k=0..74 slots=296325 split=0 ports=111 controls=9 no_new_kappa
```

The main verifier rejects nine semantic controls. Six separate test groups pass, including 3,456 exact rational head/tail basis columns across 27 source fixtures, all 86 small width-seven/eight prefix words fitting the source capacities, changed completions, wrong exterior axes and gapped/overlapping placements. Real exported-source corruption rejects before execution; changing a receipt's integer zero to Boolean false also rejects. Syntax under warnings-as-errors, source bindings, metadata and whitespace checks pass. The required `PASS_R439_BSECTION_STARS` first-example control passed on all 661 columns with eight controls; `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY` also passed.

**Unchecked obligations:** a physical width-seven provider and its helper-to-host intertwiners, correlated dirty-state realization of a whole call, owner activity beyond the source window model, H1-H5 or a replacement interface, native and full selected cold replay, all-size compilation, precision/tape and analytic transfer. The predecessor DP and builder generate the audited inputs; their optimum and endpoint are not independently re-proved here. No formal-kernel proof, hosted CI success or independent human review is claimed.

## Credit

This account's PR1307 supplied the source-level/projector argument. mightyOil/Philipp supplied PR1281's mixed-width relaxation. DreamingOfClouds supplied PR589/510/463; eumemic supplied PR555 and the carrier skeleton; DaysSky supplied PR442; Zhihao Chen supplied PR386; chafreaky and the retained geometry/audit/moment contributors retain credit. Existing source files and Apache-2.0 notices are unchanged. The new contribution is the prefix lemma, the all-75 mixed-placement application and the completion-ambiguity controls, not a new optimization of their placements.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the derivation, the implementation, the checking and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

Bind an actual width-seven provider to k=1 child0/copy0, whose host projector is exactly K_q: specify its entrance/exit maps and the helper-to-host intertwiner, then charge conversion and restoration. A future allocation that intentionally splits q-perp needs a shared completion and exact individual slot projectors; the two-completion witness provides a regression fixture. Neither follow-up is a supplier-admission conclusion from this audit.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The explicit PR1736 geometric handoff was useful after nearby packing patterns proved already covered by PR1281. A useful navigation improvement would link the mixed-width question directly to the builder's prefix layout and the `mask & 255 in {0,254}` gate, so future work distinguishes a split requiring basis data from a complete-call physical-hosting obligation.
